newsitem.title: BOSNIA: British defence minister begins Sarajevo visit.
newsitem.headline: British defence minister begins Sarajevo visit.

text.p: British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo arrived in Sarajevo on Tuesday for a visit to assess the outcome of Bosnia's first post-war elections.
He will be joined by German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, who is keen for his country's armed forces to take a more mainstream role in Bosnia if the international peacekeeping mandate is extended.

Portillo said both Britain and Germany had made "huge efforts" through the work of the NATO-led IFOR force to implement the 1995 Dayton peace accord for Bosnia and help bring some stability to the former Yugoslav republic.
"Our task now will be to assess the outcome of the elections and how best the international community and the government of Bosnia can work together for a lasting peace," said Portillo.

Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic appears close to victory in the race for Bosnia's new collective presidency, with the main Serb nationalist candidate, Momcilo Krajisnik, second and Croat Kresimir Zubak running third.
Portillo and Ruehe, who arrives on Wednesday, will together visit British and German troops on peacekeeping duties in Bosnia and Croatia.
Britain has contributed a contingent of more than 9,000 to the 58,000-strong peacekeeping force. About 4,000 German support troops are based in Croatia.
Ruehe has made clear he wants German troops to play a full role in international peacekeeping missions after decades of avoiding military involvement abroad.
Deployment of German troops to the Balkans is particularly sensitive because of Germany's brutal World War Two occupation of Yugoslavia.

Germany has said, however, that it would be prepared to contribute infantry peacekeepers with armoured vehicles to a follow-on force that could succeed the NATO-led Implementation Force (IFOR), whose mandate expires on December 20.
